problem_text:
A logistics company must dispatch a technician to perform maintenance at six critical facilities across a region.  
The facilities are positioned at the following grid coordinates:  

Facility Alpha: (3,117)  
Facility Beta: (189,20)  
Facility Gamma: (85,189)  
Facility Delta: (11,139)  
Facility Epsilon: (71,34)  
Facility Zeta: (61,195)  

Travel distances between facilities, measured in kilometers, are known:  
Alpha to Gamma: 109.1 km  
Alpha to Delta: 23.4 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 107.3 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 97.2 km  
Beta to Gamma: 198.4 km  
Beta to Delta: 214.1 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 118.8 km  
Beta to Zeta: 216.8 km  
Gamma to Delta: 89.3 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 155.6 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 24.7 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 120.9 km  
Delta to Zeta: 75.1 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 161.3 km  

Due to infrastructure limitations, no direct connection exists between Facility Alpha and Facility Beta.  
Additionally, operational restrictions require that exactly one of the following two links must be part of the circuit: the connection between Beta and Gamma, or the connection between Gamma and Delta.  

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a round‑trip route that visits each facility precisely once and returns to the origin.
